source_text: Quia nihil ea potest laudabilius aestimari, si iniquitatem ulta commissi est, si vindicavit iniuriam Dei, et quia ita consortium peccati non habuit, ut officium vindicantis assumeret iustam - dicis - esse libidinem et laudis praeconio praedicandam, si eum qui Deo non oboedivit, non illi oboediendo punivit
pass_a_gloss: Because nothing she/it is-able laudabilius aestimari, if iniquitatem ulta commissi is, if vindicavit iniuriam of-God, and because so sharing of-sin not had, so-that/as officium vindicantis assumeret iustam - you-say - to-be lust and laudis praeconio praedicandam, if him who to-God not oboedivit, not illi oboediendo punivit.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Lust is just and should be publicly praised if, by refusing to obey him, it punished the person who did not obey God.
Nothing can be considered more praiseworthy if it avenged the injustice of the offense, vindicated the wrong done to God, and had so little partnership in sin that it assumed the office of avenger.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
